chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Mukan, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Sara, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: A believer will not be a true believer until he is fearful and hopeful; and he will not be fearful and hopeful until he acts for what he fears and hopes for.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a believer to be considered truly faithful according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that true faith requires a dynamic equilibrium between fear (khawf) and hope (rajā’), preventing the extremes of despair and complacency. Crucially, he links these spiritual states to active practice, asserting that one only truly fears and hopes when their actions are aligned with the consequences they anticipate, a concept central to Shia theological psychology. This hadith underscores the inseparable bond between internal conviction and external righteous deeds in achieving spiritual perfection.
